task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific browser-fingerprint value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after click-pulse routing, armed/global gating, browser runtime signal collection and tuple preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable fingerprint rather than merely collecting signals, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: WeakMap-backed synthetic pointer channel after browser runtime signal collection

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
Several high-value function names remain readable in the captured bundle, so the intended hard part is semantic disambiguation among browser-fingerprint candidate functions, not name recovery alone.
Navigator, screen, timezone, canvas, audio-codec and storage capability signals are collected in separate helpers and then encoded into a shuffled tuple.
The target fingerprint is carried through a 3104-step state-machine transit and a runtime-selected reducer before console output.
The probe route selects its active reducer slot only after click-pulse armed/global gating and browser runtime signal capture.
The reducer table contains 32 entries; only slot 23 is selected by the live global-scan path.

The scan path crosses click pulse creation, lane resolution, armed/global gating, six browser-signal collectors, field obfuscation, tuple construction, idle/resize/focus scheduling, a WeakMap synthetic pointer channel, middleware compose, state-machine trampoline, reducer selection, fingerprint construction and sink wrapping.
Twelve same-interaction console and dataset shadows expose valid-looking fp_-prefixed browser_fingerprint values that do not feed the target action.
The deployed bundle contains 44 themed x-modules and 25 vendor-noise modules, while the reducer table exposes 31 inactive fingerprint reducers structurally similar to the live slot-23 reducer.
The target value is separated from the visible click by Promise continuation, requestIdleCallback fallback, ResizeObserver, focus event and synthetic pointer-channel boundaries.
The state-machine trampoline runs 3104 steps over the browser-signal tuple; the transit value changes the active reducer output.
The final console sink receives an already-constructed browser_fingerprint value, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.
The active reducer is stored in a Map and retrieved via the slot ID provided by o0/o2 at runtime, making static selection non-trivial.

behavior_category.reason: The observable is a stable fp_-prefixed identifier constructed primarily from navigator, screen, timezone, canvas, audio-codec and storage-capability signals plus explicit probe settings. It is not a request field rewrite, request proof, UI-state code or byte-array payload.

near_categories.why_not: No target fetch request or request header is emitted; the observable is a console-visible browser identity summary.
The value has no request-authentication, seal or proof semantics.
Probe controls influence the result, but the dominant inputs are browser environment and capability signals rather than reusable UI state.
The target is a fingerprint identifier rather than a binary payload or byte-buffer transformation.

metadata_partitioning_notes.reason: The physical case layout separates agent-visible materials from maintainer-only oracle, build metadata, source and scripts.
